rows: F-1 student visa, MS or PhD
A biotechnology, bioinformatics, or bioengineering master's (usually 1.5-2 years) or a funded PhD at a US university.
Most biotech master's programs are not funded. A PhD often is, through a research or teaching assistantship, but selection is competitive and the commitment runs 4-6 years.
12 months of work authorisation tied to your degree, usable with any employer in your field.
This is your first real job-hunt window, and it starts counting down the day you get approved, whether or not you have found an employer yet.
An additional 24 months (36 months total) if your program's CIP code is STEM-designated, most biotechnology, bioinformatics, and biomedical-engineering programs qualify.
Requires your employer to be enrolled in E-Verify and to file specific paperwork. Confirm your exact program's CIP code with the university before assuming eligibility.

A wage-weighted lottery. As of the FY2027 cycle, entry-level (Level I wage) positions, where most fresh graduates land, get roughly 15% selection odds; Level II is roughly 31%, Level III roughly 46%, Level IV roughly 61%.
You typically get one attempt per year, for up to three attempts during your OPT window. Missing the lottery every year is a real, common outcome, not an edge case.

items.heading: Build a Country
items.text: Build a country-specific resume or CV format before you apply for anything, a US resume, a Canadian resume, and a UK-style CV are genuinely different documents, and recruiters notice immediately when you have not adapted.

items.heading: Build a Target
items.text: Build a target-employer list specific to your lane and city cluster. The clusters named in each country section above are a starting point for that list, not the whole list.

items.heading: Track Real Open Roles Months
items.text: Track real open roles months before you need one, using LinkedIn and sector-specific boards such as BioSpace in the US and the regional equivalents in Canada and Australia, do not start the job search only after graduation.

items.heading: Reach Out to Alumni From
items.text: Reach out to alumni from your specific program who already work in your target country. One specific, well-researched message that references their actual work beats a mass "please guide me" post every time.

items.heading: The Dominant, Realistic Route
items.text: The dominant, realistic route. Structured post-study work windows exist specifically for graduates in all three countries, so employers can sponsor you without needing a prior local work history.

items.heading: International Recruiters Expect This Path
items.text: International recruiters expect this path. It is what their hiring pipelines and visa paperwork are actually built around.

items.heading: Still Requires a Real Budget,
items.text: Still requires a real budget, a real lane decision, and a real backup plan, it is a route, not a guarantee.
